cards.b: Taking part in sport or physical activity.

cards.f: Why do fewer girls take part in some sports?
cards.b: Fewer role models and media coverage, stereotypes, peer pressure and fewer female teams or sessions.
Inaccessible facilities, costly specialist equipment, lack of trained coaches, limited provision.
Cost of kit, membership and travel can stop lower-income groups taking part.
Running sport as a business to make money.
The link between sport, sponsorship and the media: each benefits from the others.
Support, usually money, from a business in return for advertising.

cards.f: Advantage of sponsorship to a performer
cards.b: Funds training, equipment and travel, allowing full-time training.
Pressure to win, sponsor can withdraw, and sponsors may influence the sport.
Raises awareness and participation, shows role models, brings in income.
Playing fairly, respecting the rules, opponents and officials.
Bending the rules without breaking them to gain an advantage, e.g. time-wasting.
Behaviour that breaks the rules or accepted norms, e.g. cheating, drug use, violence.
Mean: total ÷ number of values. Range: highest − lowest.
Reliable: consistent when repeated. Valid: measures what it claims to measure.

short.q: Explain how role models can increase participation.
short.model: Successful athletes inspire people to try the sport, and people copy what they see. This is stronger when role models are from under-represented groups.

short.q: Give two disadvantages of commercialisation for spectators.
short.model: Ticket and TV subscription prices rise, and kick-off times may be changed to suit television.

short.q: Explain why a bigger sample makes data more reliable.
short.model: A larger sample is more representative and reduces the effect of unusual results, so results are more consistent.

short.q: A club had 60 members in 2021 and 72 in 2024. Calculate the percentage increase.
Give two ways of controlling violence by spectators.
short.model: Use stewards, CCTV and segregate rival fans. Ban alcohol and issue banning orders for offenders.
